Setup, the front page is the case file

Beat 1 · Setup

Talk track

IND Forge is the app preclinical teams use to build the IND, the Investigational New Drug application, submitted to the FDA before any human dose. The front page is their case file: program identity up top, four tabs underneath for safety, translatability, dose, and the final package.

Presenter notes

  • Define IND once. Everything after assumes the audience has it.
  • Walk the front page. Header strip on top is program identity. The four tabs are the four chapters of the IND. That's the mental model.
  • Land the three asks (safe, effective, defensible dose). The whole talk hangs on these.
Look at: The Data Sources card showing RNA-seq (18,432 transcripts), proteomics (4,127 proteins), metabolomics (612 metabolites), all on the preclinical-omics NetApp volume; the amber residency callout
Beat 2 of 7 8s · cumulative 0:21

Translatability Review, three omics types pinned on-prem

Beat 2 · Translatability Review inputs

Talk track

The Translatability Review pulls three omics types, RNA-seq, proteomics, metabolomics, all pinned on-prem by IT policy. HPC-shaped workload across the animal cohort.

Presenter notes

  • Name the three data types out loud. RNA-seq, proteomics, metabolomics. The audience needs to hear "multi-omics" is real, not marketing.
  • Volumes matter. 18k + 4k + 600 features × 40 animals × bootstraps. That's why HPC.
  • Point at the amber callout. Don't paraphrase the residency rule, let the screen say it.
Look at: Cambridge HPC selected as RECOMMENDED, the green compliance pills (Animal-omics data residency · Internal IT approved · GLP audit chain preserved), the SLURM array job framing
Beat 3 of 7 12s · cumulative 0:33

The SLURM moment, compute moves to the data

Beat 3 · The SLURM moment

Talk track

Hit Run. Here's the SLURM moment. The job routes to the on-prem Cambridge HPC, where the data already lives, as a SLURM array job. Compliance pills confirm: residency held, IT approved, GLP audit chain preserved. The data doesn't move. The compute moves to it.

Presenter notes

  • This is the keeper line. "The data doesn't move. The compute moves to it." Pause briefly after.
  • Why SLURM specifically. Pharma HPC clusters run SLURM. Saying it signals real on-prem compute, not a marketing layer.
  • Compliance pills do the work. Don't read aloud. Let the audience see them.
  • The contrast. Today, scientists SSH in and hand-write SLURM scripts. This is the same scheduler, dispatched from the platform.
Look at: The five stat cards (8 candidates, MOFA+ 10 factors, 1000 bootstraps 95% CI, Cambridge HPC cpu-long, 134 min wall time); the translatability envelope table with CI bars and CXCL9 leading

Sweep results, eight candidates with confidence intervals

Beat 4 · Sweep results

Talk track

Eight candidates back, each with a 95% confidence interval. CXCL9 leads. No firewall crossed.

Presenter notes

  • The CI bars are the proof. Don't claim "we ran a bootstrap". Let the bars speak.
  • CXCL9 as the PD anchor. It carries forward into the dose tab.
  • 134 min · Cambridge HPC is visible top-right. Reinforces what just happened.
Look at: Inputs panel (NOAEL, allometric exponent, MABEL params), the 0.8 mg recommended FIH dose card, the calculations-overview block with formulas + citations (FDA 2005, EMA 2017, ICH M3), and the exposure-response chart with MABEL / EC50 / NOAEL plot-lines
Beat 5 of 7 13s · cumulative 0:53

PK/PD & FIH Dose, inputs, recommendation, math, exposure response

Beat 5 · PK/PD & FIH Dose

Talk track

PK/PD tab. Inputs are editable, the FIH dose recomputes live: 0.8 mg, MABEL-controlled. Every step shows the formula and citation, FDA 2005, EMA 2017, ICH M3. The exposure-response chart shows where MABEL, EC50, and NOAEL sit relative to the starting dose.

Presenter notes

  • Editable inputs are the hook. Nothing is hard-coded. A pharmacometrician trusts a tool that lets them change assumptions.
  • Walk the math chain in order: NOAEL → HED (allometric scaling) → MRSD (safety factor 10) → MABEL (10% RO per EMA) → exposure margin. Each row shows the formula and the citation. That's explainability.
  • MABEL beat MRSD here. Lower of the two wins. Worth one beat of voice on "the lower value is selected" if you have time.
  • Exposure-response chart is the visual close. The starting dose sits well left of EC50 and NOAEL. Safety margin made visible.
Look at: The 21 CFR §312.23 dossier view with five in-scope sections (purple) and eight external sections; the "X / 5 ready" progress meter; the per-section evidence chain (GLP studies, computations) and Done / Not started status badges
Beat 6 of 7 6s · cumulative 0:59

IND Package, what's tracked and how it shapes up

Beat 6 · IND Package

Talk track

The package view: thirteen sections per 21 CFR §312.23, five authored here, the rest owned elsewhere. Status rolls up as evidence attaches.

Presenter notes

  • 5 / 13 is the right framing. IND Forge owns the preclinical piece, not the whole submission. That honesty earns trust.
  • Evidence chain is the story. Pharm/Tox section links straight to GLP-001, GLP-002, GLP-003, GLP-004 and the live dose calculation. No copy-paste.
  • Progress meter at the top tells the program lead at a glance how close they are to filing.
Look at: The Generate IND package drawer scrolled to the bottom, showing Download .pdf, Download .docx, and Send to Veeva Vault RIM; the 21 CFR Part 11 audit-trail row above it
Beat 7 of 7 7s · cumulative 1:06

Generate the package and send it to Veeva Vault RIM

Beat 7 · Generate and submit

Talk track

Click Generate, the drawer assembles from on-screen state, 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail captured. Scroll to the bottom: send straight to Veeva Vault RIM. One audit chain, no egress.

Presenter notes

  • Generate is the payoff. Everything from beats 2 through 6 lands here as one assembled artifact.
  • 21 CFR Part 11. Snapshot ID, math kernel version, user, timestamp. Don't read all four; just say "21 CFR Part 11 compliant" and move on.
  • Veeva Vault RIM is the handoff. That's where Regulatory Affairs already lives. The data leaves IND Forge cleanly into a system the audience already knows.
  • Final keeper: "One audit chain, no egress." Stop talking after.
